title: KFC Chile files a complaint over computer fraud that diverted severance payments
date_note: Day KFC Chile filed the complaint, per The Clinic's article of the same day; the article places the fraudulent transfers in late October, so the incident itself is earlier.
summary: The Clinic reports that KFC Chile filed a complaint for computer fraud on Monday 23 November with the 4th Garantía Court of Santiago. According to the complaint as reported, severance payment lists loaded on a bank platform were replaced by fraudulent lists using the credentials of a former payroll supervisor, and the money went to two accounts that were not on the original list. KFC asks that funds still in those accounts be retained.
plain: KFC Chile says severance payments for workers were redirected to two other accounts by someone using a former payroll supervisor's login, and it has filed a court complaint.
exec: A restaurant company's payroll payments were redirected through a former employee's still-active login, according to its court complaint.
action: No action needed; for awareness. General advice: revoke the access of departing staff to payment platforms promptly.
geo_basis: court in Santiago where the complaint was filed; the article gives no victim city

evidence.quote: KFC Chile presentó este lunes una querella por fraude informático al 4° Juzgado de Garantía de Santiago
La operación se ejecutó con el usuario y clave de una exsupervisora del área de remuneraciones de KFC

validation.note: Only The Clinic was read, relayed by a fetch sub-agent because direct page fetch was denied; it relays KFC's own complaint. No second publisher or court document read.
